chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl narrated to me from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said:

I said: A woman or a slave-girl clings to me from behind while I am reclining on my side, and she moves on my back, then desire comes to her and she emits fluid. Is ghusl (ritual bath) obligatory upon her or not? He said: “Yes. If desire comes to her and she emits fluid, ghusl becomes obligatory upon her.”
As for the report narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from Fadalah, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:

I said to Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام: A man places his private part upon the woman’s private part and ejaculates—does ghusl apply to her? He said: “If any of the fluid reaches her, then let her wash it, and nothing is obligatory upon her unless he inserts it.” I said: Then if she reaches climax but he does not insert it? He said: “Ghusl is not obligatory upon her.”

key_terms.أَمْنَتْ: she reached climax or experienced emission
key_terms.يُدْخِلَهُ: that he inserts it; referring to penetration
key_terms.ٱلْغُسْلُ: the ritual bath required after janabah
key_terms.ٱلْمَاءَ: fluid referred to in the context of sexual emission

ai.seo_question: When does ghusl become obligatory upon a woman in cases of sexual arousal without intercourse?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses rulings of janabah and when ghusl becomes obligatory in cases involving sexual arousal and emission. The first report states that if a woman experiences desire and emits fluid, ghusl is obligatory upon her, while the second report states that without insertion, ghusl is not obligatory upon her even if the man ejaculates onto her.
